notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is typed 'a' inside a word and dropped at the end of a word after a lone consonant (घर ghar), but said and typed after a cluster (गर्छ garchha, भन्छ bhanchha). Speech drops it inside words too (सरकार sarkar), and typists follow speech or the letters; the skeleton drops every a between two consonants so both give one key. letters: Nepali says व as b or w as often as v (विश्व bishwa, सेवा sewa), and श ष स all as s, so each lists those spellings. छ is chh, ch or, in chat, x (छ xa). क्ष is said chh (क्षेत्र chhetra) or ksh. ङ is ng (रङ rang, सङ्ग sanga). Candrabindu is n or nothing (गाउँ gaun / gau, हुँदैन hundaina / hudaina), anusvara n, or m before a labial. ज्ञ is gy (ज्ञान gyan). skeleton: Aspirates fold to their plain letters, sh to s, z to j, f to p, w to v, q to k; aa, ee and oo to a, i and u; mb and mp to nb and np. chh, ch and x fold to c, and so do ksh, kch and ks: Nepali chat types छ as x (xa, garxu) and says क्ष as chh (क्षेत्री chhetri), so all of them give one key. On the 803 calibration pairs this changes nothing (the annotators wrote chh and ksh); it is for chat. A final a after a consonant is dropped, which covers the final inherent vowel typed or not. unwritten: A final candrabindu or anusvara after a vowel is as often left unwritten (गाउँ gau, हुँ hu), so optionalFinals names both: such a word is also keyed by the skeleton of its walk without the n, and either spelling spells it out. The dropped medial vowel is often written u (hum for हम), so alsoBetweenConsonants u, as for Hindi and Maithili.
